notes:
Summary: Lost to hyperscaler-managed endpoints (AWS/Azure/GCP). Long sales cycle; technical POC showed parity on accuracy but hyperscalers won on integration and perceived operational risk.

Recent timeline:
- 2025-09-02: Discovery call w/ Head of Data Platforms (Samir Patel) + Dir of Ops. Interest: chat support for drivers + embeddings for load docs.
- 2025-10-15: POC kickoff (2-week micro-POC) - focus on embeddings search across manifests and support chat.
- 2025-11-02: Interim POC notes - Redwood runtime performance good, latency < 120ms for typical requests in Dedicated config. Cost estimate projected ~$18k/mo (dedicated).
- 2025-12-08: Security review initial - required VPC, key management, audit retention 3 years. They asked for HSM/KMS integration.
- 2026-01-19: Procurement flagged budget concerns; finance asked for comparison vs hyperscaler managed endpoints.
- 2026-02-14: Final security dec - Security & Platform team recommend managed endpoints to avoid running customer keys on third-party infra. Quote: "We can't risk managing keys and custom network appliances right now; native cloud audit hooks are a hard requirement" (Head of Security).
- 2026-02-22: Final commercial call - Halcyon selects AWS SageMaker/Managed endpoints for faster path to compliance and lower short-term ops cost.

Decision rationale (customer words / shorthand):
- "Faster to compliance with existing AWS tooling".
- Integration: AWS native IAM + CloudTrail + KMS fit our security playbook.
- Ops: fewer moving parts for platform team; one vendor to manage.
- Cost: procurement spreadsheet showed lower TCO first 12 months with hyperscaler when factoring staff time.

Sales / POC notes (shorthand):
- Redwood technical fit: strong perf, good latency numbers in dedicated. Customer liked batching suggestions from Redwood Optimize.
- Main gap: hyperscaler's ecosystem pre-integrations (CloudTrail, Config, managed KMS) and simpler procurement flow.
- Internal champion churn: initial AI lead (Samir) left for startup in Dec; momentum slowed.

Next actions taken:
- 2026-02-25: AE sent formal exit summary + Redwood cost comparison + ask to keep door open for 6 months.
- Action item: schedule win-back outreach for Aug 2026 after fiscal refresh.

Open hints for re-engagement:
- Watch for spike in incidents or cost increases on hyperscaler run; they may re-evaluate multi-cloud/private options.
- Keep lightweight reference of Redwood security integrations (KMS/HSM patterns) and a short note on canary fallback/dual-routing play.

Attachments / refs: drive links above, security FAQ shared 2026-02-14, POChange spreadsheet (shared via Gmail thread).

Internal AE notes: "Tough loss. Good technical fit but late-cycle org changes + hyperscaler integration narrative won. Keep relationship warm — platform team friendly, procurement receptive to regular updates."
